title: Per-sender message FIFO inversion at store-back — drain the arrival queue before merging deferred messages
purpose: Ground: `docs/REVIEW-23-07.md` finding M11 (MEDIUM, concurrency/messaging), reviewed at `fd71c5e`: "Per-sender message FIFO inversion. `scheduler/execution/core.rs:442` — `store_runnable_process` appends `Executing`-deferred pending messages to the back of the scan list without first draining the arrival queue, so on a compute-only slice an older arrival message can order after a newer pending one — a BEAM ordering-guarantee violation. The debugger snapshot path drains first, showing the authors know the correct order." RE-PINNED AT `a0359a2`: NO DRIFT — `crates/beamr/src/scheduler/execution/core.rs:442` is still `for payload in metadata.pending_local_messages.drain(..) {`, inside the `ProcessSlot::Executing(metadata)` merge arm of `store_runnable_process` (:344-506, arm opens at :348). THE MECHANISM, traced end to end at the pin. A `Mailbox` (`crates/beamr/src/mailbox/mod.rs:50-55`) has TWO queues: `arrival`, a lock-free MPSC `SegQueue` that other processes push into through `MailboxSender` (:247-339), and `scan_list`, an owner-only `VecDeque` that selective receive walks. `drain_arrival` (:114-118) moves the former into the back of the latter, and every RECEIVE-side entry point calls it first (`current_message` :121-126, `remove_current_message` :137-142, `reserve_save_marker` :161-164, `set_save_pointer` :167-170, `bind_recv_marker` :179-182). `push_owned` (:208-210) does NOT — it appends straight to `scan_list`. Now the two delivery routes for the SAME sender: `SchedulerLocalSendFacility::send_local` (`crates/beamr/src/scheduler/supervision_integration.rs:919-1074`) pushes into the receiver's ARRIVAL queue when the receiver's slot is `Present` (:1004-1018, via `mailbox().sender().send(..)`), and ETF-encodes into `metadata.pending_local_messages` when the slot is `Executing` (:1025-1067, push at :1066). So: sender S sends A while R is Present -> A sits in `arrival`. R is checked out to run (slot -> `Executing`). S sends B while R runs -> B sits in `pending_local_messages`. R's slice is compute-only, so nothing ever calls a receive-side entry point and `arrival` is never drained. `store_runnable_process` then merges B with `push_owned` (:450) onto the BACK of `scan_list`, which still does not contain A. R's next `receive` calls `current_message` -> `drain_arrival` -> A lands AFTER B. R observes B before A although S sent A first: a violation of BEAM's per-sender-pair signal ordering guarantee, from ordinary two-process code, with no unusual timing required beyond the receiver being mid-slice. THE SAME INVERSION EXISTS FOR EVERY DEFERRED CATEGORY the arm merges, not just local sends: `pending_exit_messages` (:389-406), `pending_down_messages` (:407-414), `pending_io_messages` (:415-431), `pending_distribution_payloads` (:432-441), `pending_local_messages` (:442-451), `pending_ets_transfer_messages` (:452-466), `pending_udp_messages` (:467-477) and `pending_tcp_messages` (:478-487) — all of them reach the mailbox through `push_owned`/`enqueue_*_pub` after the arm has skipped the drain. THE CORRECT ORDER THE AUTHORS ALREADY KNOW, cited twice in-tree: `crates/beamr/src/replay/debugger.rs:443-456` — `record_snapshot` calls `self.process.mailbox_mut().drain_arrival()` at :451 BEFORE cloning the process, and it has to, because `impl Clone for Mailbox` (`mailbox/mod.rs:74-83`) gives the clone a FRESH EMPTY arrival queue and copies only `scan_list`; and `crates/beamr/src/process/mod.rs:562-563` — `roots_with_live_x` drains at :563 before enumerating GC roots, so arrivals are rooted. Two independent places in the tree already establish "before you touch the mailbox as a whole, drain arrivals first"; the store-back merge is the one that does not.
task:
DESIGN STANCE (decided; no fork). The fix is to restore the invariant, not to reorder the merge: BEFORE the `Executing` merge arm performs its FIRST mailbox mutation, drain the arrival queue into the scan list. Everything already in flight from a Present-slot send then precedes everything deferred during the slice, which is exactly the arrival order, and the existing per-category merge order is preserved unchanged for messages deferred within the same slice.

D1 WHY DRAIN-FIRST IS COMPLETE AND RACE-FREE (the argument the tear should check rather than re-derive). Both delivery routes take the SAME lock: `send_local` acquires the body-slot mutex (`supervision_integration.rs:935` `lock_or_recover(&entry)`) and decides Present-vs-Executing under it, and `store_runnable_process` holds that same slot lock across the whole merge and the `*slot = ProcessSlot::Present(..)` transition (`execution/core.rs:347` to :489). Therefore: any send that completed before the merge took the lock has ALREADY landed in either `arrival` or `pending_*`, and both are visible to the merge; any send that arrives after the merge releases the lock sees `Present`, goes to `arrival`, and is genuinely later. There is no window in which a message can be older than the drain yet invisible to it. A drain at the TOP of the arm is therefore sufficient — no ordering token, no sequence number, no clock comparison is needed.

D2 PLACEMENT IS EXACT. The drain must precede `pending_exit_messages` (:389), which is the first mutation, NOT merely precede :442. Placing it at :442 would fix local sends and leave exit/DOWN/IO/distribution signals inverted. The drain belongs immediately inside the `if let ProcessSlot::Executing(metadata) = &mut *slot` arm, before the metadata-restoration block if that block can touch the mailbox and otherwise before the first `enqueue_*`/`push_owned`. State the chosen point and the reason in a comment.

D3 COST. `drain_arrival` is an owner-only pop loop over a `SegQueue` that the receive path was going to run anyway on the next receive; the merge already holds the lock. The added work is zero-allocation and bounded by the number of messages that arrived during the slice. There is no new lock, no new wake path, no timer, no allocation. NO-POLLING is not engaged.

D4 SCOPE FENCE — THE ADJACENT REVIEW FINDING IS NOT REOPENED. The review's M12 (`supervision_integration.rs:1004`, local send to a Present receiver silently dropping on `HeapFull`, plus the free-variable-closure ETF drop noted in the code comment at :1049-1060) is a DIFFERENT defect on the same function. This brief changes ordering only. If the red test happens to observe a drop, record it and route it to M12's lane; do not fix it here.

D5 THE ORDERING CONTRACT BECOMES CODE. The invariant is currently implicit in three scattered call sites. This brief writes it down where it can be enforced: a doc comment on `Mailbox::push_owned` (`mailbox/mod.rs:207-210`) stating that it appends to the owner-side scan list and therefore MUST NOT be called on a mailbox with undrained arrivals unless the caller has already drained, and a comment at the merge arm naming the guarantee (per-sender FIFO across the Present/Executing route split) with the `debugger.rs:451` and `process/mod.rs:563` precedents cited. A future deferred category then inherits the rule instead of rediscovering the bug.

requirements.title: RED probe: a deterministic interleaving that proves the inversion
requirements.spec: Per the mechanism trace: a single-threaded, timing-free test driven entirely through the scheduler's own test seams, added to `crates/beamr/src/scheduler/supervision_tests.rs` (or a new sibling `message_order_tests.rs` wired into `scheduler/mod.rs` under the same `#[cfg(test)]` gate). The seams already exist and are used by `reference_message_to_executing_receiver_round_trips_via_etf` (`supervision_tests.rs:1049-1103`), which is the model to follow: `make_shared_state()` (:251), `insert_process(&shared, pid)` (:24-41), `supervision_integration::build_native_services(&shared, NamespaceId::DEFAULT)` to obtain the real `LocalSendFacility`, `make_executing(&shared, pid)` (:128-167) to move the receiver's slot to `Executing` and hand back the checked-out `Process`, and `store_runnable_process(&shared, receiver)` to run the merge. SEQUENCE: (1) insert sender and receiver; (2) with the receiver PRESENT, `facility.send_local(..)` message A (a distinct atom, so no heap layout question arises); (3) `make_executing(&shared, receiver_pid)`; (4) `facility.send_local(..)` message B; (5) `store_runnable_process`; (6) read the receiver's mailbox IN ORDER — `drain_arrival()` then walk `scan_iter()` (`mailbox/mod.rs:225-227`, `pub(crate)`, reachable from an in-crate test) — and assert the sequence is exactly [A, B]. Add a second leg proving the same for a cross-category pair (an arrival A followed by a slice-deferred EXIT or DOWN signal), so the fix is pinned at the FIRST mutation point and not just at `pending_local_messages`.
acceptance: Pre-fix RED: the observed order is [B, A] and the assertion fails with both terms named in the message — recorded as the fail-first evidence
Post-fix GREEN: the observed order is [A, B] on both legs

FULLY DETERMINISTIC: no threads, no sleeps, no deadlines, no retries; the interleaving is produced by calling the seams in a fixed sequence on one thread, so the test cannot flake and does not depend on scheduler timing
The test asserts the WHOLE ordered sequence, not just the front element — `read_mailbox_tuple` (:43-58) only reads the head and is insufficient; add or use an ordered-terms helper
Ten consecutive isolated runs are stable in both directions

requirements.title: Drain arrivals at the top of the Executing merge arm
requirements.spec: Per D1/D2: in `store_runnable_process` (`crates/beamr/src/scheduler/execution/core.rs:344-506`), inside the `ProcessSlot::Executing(metadata)` arm, call `process.mailbox_mut().drain_arrival()` before the first mailbox mutation — i.e. before the `pending_exit_messages` loop at :389 — so every message that arrived through the Present route during or before the slice is already in the scan list when the deferred categories are appended. No other line of the merge changes: the metadata restoration (:349-388), the per-category merge ORDER (:389-487) and the `*slot = ProcessSlot::Present(..)` transition (:489) are byte-preserved.
acceptance: The drain is the first mailbox-touching statement in the arm, and a comment states WHY it must precede `pending_exit_messages` rather than merely `pending_local_messages` (D2)

The lock-serialisation argument (D1) is recorded in that comment: both send routes decide under the same slot mutex the merge holds, so a drain at the top is sufficient and no ordering token is needed

Relative order WITHIN a slice is unchanged: the existing category sequence (exit, down, io, distribution, local, ets-transfer, udp, tcp) is preserved exactly, and no category is reordered to work around the bug
No new allocation, no new lock, no new wake path, no timer — the diff adds one call and comments

The full existing scheduler suite passes unmodified, including `reference_message_to_executing_receiver_round_trips_via_etf` (`supervision_tests.rs:1049`), the exit/DOWN mid-slice tests (:811-916) and the readiness/teardown suites

requirements.title: Write the ordering contract down where the next deferred category will read it
requirements.spec: Per D5: doc-comment `Mailbox::push_owned` (`crates/beamr/src/mailbox/mod.rs:207-210`) with the precondition that it appends to the owner-only scan list and so must not be used on a mailbox with undrained arrivals unless the caller drained first, naming the two existing precedents (`replay/debugger.rs:451`, `process/mod.rs:563`) and the reason the debugger one is load-bearing (`impl Clone for Mailbox` at :74-83 gives the clone an EMPTY arrival queue). Mirror the guarantee at the merge arm in `execution/core.rs` in the terms BEAM uses: messages from one sender to one receiver are observed in send order, regardless of which side of the Present/Executing route split each took.
acceptance: A reader adding a ninth `pending_*` category to `ProcessMetadata` encounters the rule at both the mailbox API and the merge site
The comments state the guarantee and its scope precisely — per SENDER-RECEIVER PAIR ordering, not a global mailbox total order (beamr must not claim more than BEAM does)
No behaviour change in this requirement: documentation and comments only

boundaries: ORDERING ONLY. The merge's per-category sequence, the ETF encode/decode round trip for deferred local and distribution messages, the Lamport-clock deferral posture documented at `supervision_integration.rs:1031-1038`, the `wake_process` call after the lock is released (:1072), and the `Absent`/vanished-entry arms of `store_runnable_process` (:490-505) are all UNCHANGED. Anything that alters WHICH messages are delivered, or when a process is woken, is a STOP.

M12 IS ADJACENT, NOT REOPENED: the `HeapFull` silent drop on the Present path (`supervision_integration.rs:1004-1018`) and the free-variable-closure ETF drop (:1049-1064) are a different finding with a different lane. If R1 observes a drop, record it and route it; do not fix it here.

NO NEW SYNCHRONISATION: no ordering token, no sequence number, no per-message timestamp, no second lock, no atomic. The slot mutex already serialises both routes (D1); a fix that adds machinery is a sign the argument was not read.

SELECTIVE-RECEIVE STATE IS UNTOUCHED: `save_pointer`, `recv_marker`, `reserve_save_marker`/`set_save_pointer`/`use_recv_marker` semantics and the OTP receive-marker tests must be byte-identical. Draining at store-back appends to the scan list exactly as the next receive would have done, so no save pointer moves.

WASM32: `scheduler/execution/**` and `scheduler/supervision_integration.rs` are `#[cfg(feature = "threads")]` (`scheduler/mod.rs:117-118` and neighbours) and never compile under the cooperative wasm32 closure. `crates/beamr/src/mailbox/mod.rs` IS ungated and DOES compile there, so R3's doc-comment edit must keep both wasm32 check legs green; it adds no code. The beamr-wasm 80-test count and its three CI carriers are untouched.

ZERO new `#[allow]`; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`; no new `_ =>` catch-all arms; `crates/beamr/src/loader/encode/**` untouchable; no new config knobs; NO-POLLING is not engaged (no thread, timer or wake path is added or changed).
House LOC bar: `scheduler/execution/core.rs` is 1,739 lines at the pin, already far over the advisory. This brief adds one call and comments and MUST NOT be used as a vehicle for splitting the file.
verification: Full release battery at the final head: the committed 5-leg `gates.json` run (`fmt`; fresh `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` with `cargo clean -p beamr` and the Compiling line captured; `wasm32-check`; `wasm-tests` with the exact 80-passed carrier unchanged; `tests` workspace-wide), plus the cooperative wasm closure leg (`cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p beamr --no-default-features --features cooperative,json --locked`) and a prohibition grep sweep run through `git -c diff.external= diff --no-ext-diff`. Isolation: the new ordering tests 10x, plus 10x on the pre-existing scheduler suite given how ordering-sensitive it is. FAIL-FIRST, recorded-and-reverted: (a) remove R2's drain -> R1 goes red on both legs with the [B, A] order named -> restore; (b) move R2's drain from the top of the arm down to just above `pending_local_messages` (:442) -> R1's cross-category leg goes red while the local-send leg stays green, proving the D2 placement argument -> restore. PIN-SHIFT RE-VERIFY at the actual build base (pinned at `a0359a2`): re-read `scheduler/execution/core.rs:344-506` (arm open :348, first mutation :389, cited line :442, transition :489); `mailbox/mod.rs:50-55`, :74-83, :114-118, :121-126, :207-210, :225-232; `supervision_integration.rs:919-1074` (Present arm :1004-1018, Executing arm :1025-1067); `replay/debugger.rs:443-456`; `process/mod.rs:562-563`; and the test seams `supervision_tests.rs:24-58`, :128-167, :251, :1049-1103. Handoff carries: the exact drain placement as landed with the D2 reason, the observed pre-fix and post-fix orders for both legs, and any M12-class drop observed while building (routed, not fixed).
